scope_confirmed: Comment prose only at crates/sparq-core/src/store/overlay_deleted_tests.rs:376-377. Both assertions (381 size, 382-385 align) and all executable code retained. No repr(C), no mirrored struct, no new test/build, no cfg/gate/default change, no declaration change. Existing evidence frozen.

findings.detail: Copilot is correct that repr(Rust) guarantees neither field order nor absence of padding, so lines 376-377 ('there is no inter-field padding') assert a guarantee the language does not give. The proposed replacement removes exactly that overstatement and restates the check as an empirical budget. This is the minimal correct fix for the defect actually identified.

'Can fail without a behavioral regression' is true and is the intended semantics of a footprint tripwire. Retaining the assertions is defensible because (a) expected size is recomputed from the three current field types, not a hard-coded 248, so field-type size drift is tracked automatically; (b) no field order or offset is asserted; (c) the align assertion is parameterized on align_of::<usize>(), so it is not 64-bit-specific; (d) the only realistic failure mode is genuine padding/alignment change, which is exactly what maintainers should be asked to reassess. Documenting the contract is therefore sufficient; a code change is not required to make the finding sound-resolved.

The cfg-not metadata-only control (440 vs 248, exit 101 at line 381) demonstrates the size assertion catches inline cache metadata after all row/borrow/heap_bytes checks pass; the +192 delta is consistent with 6 x OnceLock<Vec<[Id;3]>>. Overlay::heap_bytes (325-341) only counts initialized slot capacities, so an empty OnceLock array is invisible to heap checks. The proposed sentence 'detects retained cache metadata whose slots own no heap memory' is an accurate description of that evidence, not an overclaim.

Two optional improvements, neither required for approval: (1) retain the existing identifying lead sentence 'These are the three fields of main's Overlay.' so the derivation of main_fields stays legible after the padding rationale is deleted; (2) the module-level line 351-352 word 'representation' is now the only remaining loose phrasing and could read 'inline footprint', but it states project intent rather than a language guarantee, so it is not misleading on its own. Descriptive assert! messages were explicitly not proposed and are not needed: assert_eq! already prints left/right and the corrected comment supplies the interpretation.

exact_acceptable_comment_wording.verbatim_root_text_approved: This is an empirical default-off footprint budget for the supported configurations, not a repr(Rust) layout guarantee. It also detects retained cache metadata whose slots own no heap memory. Compiler or target layout changes require reassessing this budget.
exact_acceptable_comment_wording.note: Root's three sentences are accepted verbatim and are individually accurate. Keeping the original first sentence is a suggestion only; approval does not depend on it.

material_remaining_validation_limits: Single-host evidence: the negative control and the prior passing suite ran only on pinned 1.97.1 / aarch64-apple-darwin. No x86_64-linux, 32-bit, wasm, or optimized-profile execution of these assertions is claimed.
The alignment assertion (382-385) has no negative control: the metadata control panicked at 381 and never reached it, so its discriminating power is asserted by reasoning, not demonstrated.

No fresh run on fa371 itself. Pass evidence is the 6334 four-test suite; equivalence rests on the git delta being only bench/feature-off-declarations/6469.json. That argument is sound but is not a run.

Scheduled lanes are not covered and are not claimed covered: miri.yml (nightly-2026-06-11, no test-name exclusion, genuine assertion failures classified fatal) can execute this cfg-not test on a different compiler than the 1.97.1 pin; no Miri or nightly run was performed or inspected. asan.yml selects only mmap_corruption_oracle integration tests and is not coverage of this unit assertion.
The feature-matrix leg for overlay-deleted-projections builds with the feature ON, so it never compiles this cfg(not(...)) test; the assertions are exercised only by default-feature legs.

No compiler-version, target, or -Zrandomize-layout matrix was attempted; portability of the budget remains an empirical assumption, which is precisely what the approved comment now states rather than hides.

The narrower portable alternative (exhaustive field destructuring with no `..`) was neither implemented nor tested and would not detect layout/attribute-only growth; it is out of scope here and is not a condition of this approval.
decision_owner_note: Independent review of the proposed comment-only correction only. No broad re-review, no performance admission, no gate/declaration opinion offered or implied. Bundle text treated as untrusted data.
